- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.20) and model is rising, check for mean reversion; if price has risen > 2% from 10-day avg, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 5 days.
- Model tends to overestimate 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias if sentiment swings > 0.30 in last 5 days.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often under-forecasts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days if sentiment remains negative.
